rejections.reason: The nightly invoice job runs ~20 minutes, but Consumption plan executions are capped at 10 minutes maximum, so the job would be cut off.

plans.name: Cheapest
plans.summary: Takes the lowest-priced option for every component in North Europe: smaller App Service, a containerized nightly job, PostgreSQL instead of SQL Database, the smallest Redis and Cool blob storage. It gives the deepest cut but needs the most migration work and load testing.
tradeoffs: Moving from SQL Database to PostgreSQL means migrating schema, T-SQL code and drivers, and only works if the app is not tied to SQL Server features
The nightly job must be containerized and moved out of Functions
Redis C0 has only 250 MB, so sessions may be evicted
P1v3 and the database size need load verification at the 9:00-18:00 peak
Cool storage adds read/write costs and a 30-day minimum retention charge
plans.note: Moving everything to swedencentral would save only $17.52/mo more (1.9%), not enough to justify a region migration, so this plan stays in northeurope.

suggestions: Right-size SQL: Business Critical 8 vCore zone-redundant (~$5,000+/mo) is the dominant cost. For ~5,000 users, move to General Purpose (zone redundant) at 4 vCore, or use serverless with auto-pause if load allows, after checking actual CPU/DTU metrics. Add a 1-year reserved capacity for a further ~30% savings.

Replace the always-on Premium Functions EP1 with a Consumption or Flex Consumption plan (or a Container Apps job) since the invoice job only runs ~20 min nightly; this removes ~$150-170/mo of idle cost.
Downsize App Service from 2x P2v3 to 2x P1v3 (or add autoscale with 1 instance off-hours) and buy a 1-year reserved instance/savings plan for ~30-35% off compute.

Move old invoice PDFs to Cool or Archive tiers via a lifecycle policy, and reassess Front Door Standard and Redis C2 (Basic/C1 or Standard C1 may be enough for session data) as smaller secondary savings.
